newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ROMATEX SAYS ANY BID WILL BE BELOW 330 CTS.
newsitem.headline: ROMATEX SAYS ANY BID WILL BE BELOW 330 CTS.

text.p: South African clothing and textile firm Romatex Ltd and its parent C.G. Smith Ltd said in a joint statement on Thursday that any bid for the company would be at less than 330 cents a share.

"The boards of C.G Smith and Romatex wish to advise Romatex shareholders that should a transaction be concluded it will be implemented at a price below the market price of 330 cents per Romatex ordinary share which was the price ruling on the JSE at the close of business on Friday, 13 September 1996," a statement said.

Shares in Romatex, which is 60 percent-owned by C.G. Smith and is the country's second-largest listed textiles firm, have surged this week following news that the country's biggest textile concern, Consolidated Frame Textiles Ltd (Confram), was weighing a takeover.
Romatex shares closed on Wednesday at 550 cents.

C.G. Smith Ltd said on Monday it was engaged in discussions regarding its stake in Romatex Ltd . At the same time, Confram also said it was in talks which could have an impact on its share price and that of parent Frame Group Holdings Ltd.
Mike Hankinson, managing director of Romatex, told Reuters on Tuesday that talks on Confram taking control of his company were at an advanced stage.
He said the Competition Board would have to approve the deal, but he did not foresee any problems obtaining the watchdog body's approval.
In addition to C.G. Smith's stake, analysts believe a further 20 percent of Romatex could be bought from Associated Furniture Companies Ltd .
Dealers and analysts have welcomed the link-up in the beleagured textile sector, arguing both companies would save on overheads and on manufacturing plants.
